parsed.summary: Fix integers d ≥ 4 and 2 ≤ n ≤ d−2, and constants C_AD ≥ 1 and C_R ≥ 0. The Lean statement says there exist θ > 0 and M ≥ 0 that work for every regular (Radon) Borel measure μ on ℝ^d satisfying two conditions: n-AD regularity with constant C_AD, and the uniform L² bound C_R for all hard truncations of the kernel (x−y)/|x−y|^{n+1}. For such μ, every x ∈ supp μ and every 0 < r ≤ diam(supp μ) admit an M-Lipschitz map g from the Euclidean n-ball B(0,r) into ℝ^d with μ(B(x,r) ∩ g(B)) ≥ θ rⁿ. This matches the excerpted Theorem 1.3 with class-uniform constants. The main caveat is that Definition 1.2 and condition (1.2) are not in the excerpt, so the exact conventions (μ versus Hⁿ|E, r ≤ diam versus r < diam, open versus closed balls) cannot be fully checked, though each plausible variant is equivalent up to constants.

glossary.plain: 0 < r ≤ diam(supp μ), where diam is the extended diameter (∞ allowed; 0 if the support is empty or a single point)
glossary.note: Matches the range in (1.4). The degenerate case D_E = 0 makes the conclusion vacuous, as the paper notes.

glossary.plain: K_n(x−y) = (x−y)/|x−y|^{n+1}, with value 0 on the diagonal (Lean inverse of 0 is 0)
glossary.note: Any normalizing constant is absorbed into C_R.

glossary.plain: R_{μ,ε} f(x) = ∫_{|x−y|>ε} f(y) K_n(x−y) dμ(y), as a Bochner integral (equal to 0 if not integrable)
glossary.standard_concept: hard ε-truncation of the Riesz transform
glossary.note: Lemma 1.4 shows absolute convergence for AD-regular μ with D_E > 0 and f ∈ L², so the junk value does not arise.

glossary.plain: C ≥ 1 and, for x ∈ supp μ and 0 < r ≤ diam(supp μ), rⁿ/C ≤ μ(B(x,r)) ≤ C rⁿ, with open balls
glossary.note: The upper bound is only required at support points and admissible radii; Lemma 1.4 recovers the global bound.

glossary.plain: For all ε > 0 and f ∈ L²(μ): R_{μ,ε} f ∈ L²(μ; ℝ^d) and ‖R_{μ,ε} f‖₂ ≤ C_R ‖f‖₂
glossary.standard_concept: uniform L² boundedness over hard truncations, condition (1.2)
glossary.note: The text of (1.2) is not in the excerpt; this matches the abstract's description.

glossary.plain: For x ∈ supp μ and 0 < r ≤ diam(supp μ), there is an M-Lipschitz g : B_{ℝⁿ}(0,r) → ℝ^d with μ(B(x,r) ∩ g(B)) ≥ θ rⁿ
glossary.standard_concept: big pieces of Lipschitz images of balls (uniform rectifiability, Definition 1.2)
glossary.note: Mass is measured by μ rather than possibly Hⁿ|E. These are comparable for AD-regular μ with constants depending on C_AD, n and d. Definition 1.2 is not in the excerpt.

glossary.plain: ∀ d, n with 2 ≤ n ≤ d−2 (d ≥ 4), ∀ C_AD ≥ 1, ∀ C_R, ∃ θ > 0, ∃ M, ∀ regular μ that are AD(C_AD) and Riesz(C_R) bounded, the ball-image conclusion holds
glossary.standard_concept: Theorem 1.3 with constants depending only on d, n, C_AD, C_R

lean_claims.plain: Let d, n ∈ ℕ with d ≥ 4, n ≥ 2, n+2 ≤ d, and let C_AD ≥ 1 and C_R ≥ 0. Then there exist θ > 0 and M ≥ 0 with the following property. For every regular Borel measure μ on ℝ^d satisfying, for x ∈ supp μ and 0 < r ≤ diam supp μ, the bounds rⁿ/C_AD ≤ μ(B(x,r)) ≤ C_AD rⁿ, and satisfying ‖R_{μ,ε} f‖_{L²(μ)} ≤ C_R ‖f‖_{L²(μ)} with R_{μ,ε} f ∈ L² for all ε > 0 and f ∈ L²(μ): for every such x and r there is an M-Lipschitz g from the open n-ball of radius r into ℝ^d with μ(B(x,r) ∩ g(B)) ≥ θ rⁿ.

paper_claims.plain: For d ≥ 4 and 2 ≤ n ≤ d−2, an n-AD-regular Radon measure on ℝ^d with uniformly L²-bounded hard truncations of the Riesz transform (1.2) is uniformly n-rectifiable (big pieces of Lipschitz images of balls, Definition 1.2), with θ and M depending only on d, n, C_AD and C_R.

coverage.why: Same dimension range, hypotheses, uniform quantifier order (constants chosen before μ, x and r) and ball-image conclusion, up to conventions in Definition 1.2 that are not in the excerpt.
Corollaries are not part of the target.

flags.explanation: Definition 1.2 is not in the excerpt. It may measure E ∩ B(x,r) ∩ g(B) with Hⁿ rather than μ, use closed balls, or use r < diam E. For AD-regular μ these variants are equivalent up to constants depending only on C_AD, n and d. The class-uniform form therefore matches.
flags.probe_idea: Prove that for ADRegularWithConstant n C μ, μ ≤ c(C,n,d)·Hⁿ restricted to supp μ and conversely, so the μ and Hⁿ versions of the conclusion are interchangeable.

flags.explanation: The Bochner integral returns 0 when the integrand is not integrable. Lemma 1.4 gives absolute convergence for AD-regular μ with D_E > 0 and f ∈ L², so the junk value should never be used. In the degenerate case D_E = 0 the conclusion is vacuous.
flags.probe_idea: Prove ∀ x ε > 0, MemLp f 2 μ → Integrable (fun y => f y • kernel n x y) (μ.restrict {y | ε < dist x y}) under ADRegularWithConstant with 0 < ediam μ.support.

lint_verdicts.why: Comparing ofReal r with the extended diameter correctly encodes r ≤ diam, including diam = ∞.
There is no natural-number subtraction here; the diagonal value of 0 matches the paper's convention of setting the integrand to zero on the diagonal.
Lemma 1.4 guarantees absolute convergence for AD-regular μ and f ∈ L², so the junk 0 never occurs in the relevant cases.
C ≥ 1 is required in the same definition, so there is no division by zero.
r > 0 and C ≥ 1 make ofReal faithful.
This is the standard eLpNorm operator-norm bound, and finiteness of the output norm is also required via MemLp.
θ > 0 and r > 0, so ofReal(θ rⁿ) is a positive real lower bound.
